correctness.rationale: In a primitive rank-one factorization A=cuvᵀ, use the primitive generator u of the rational image line and divide the coordinate row by its content c. Then AXA=c(vᵀXu)A, so AXA=A forces c=1; conversely primitivity of u and v allows Xu=w with vᵀw=1. A unimodular basis with first vector u gives B(t,b) with primitive row. Any intertwinor preserves its primitive image line, so its form [ε,m;0,δ] gives b′=εtm+εδb, both necessary and sufficient; t=0 gives b=±1 and one class. Independently, a nonzero nilpotent N has the form ℓ(r,s)ᵀ(−s,r) with gcd(r,s)=1 and ℓ integral. Then det(B−N)=−ℓs(tr+bs); unimodularity is possible exactly for b≡±1 mod |t|, or |b|=1 at t=0. N=0 cannot work since B is singular. Thus the criterion does select one orbit, including moduli 1 and 2. For n>2 the sign action on units has no fixed points. Totient multiplicativity and the prime-power formula give φ(n)≤2 precisely at n=1,2,3,4,6; along primes p≥5 the proportion is 2/(p−1). I inspected the frozen code and its recorded CHECK_OK: it only tests the conjugation formula on a finite box and sign orbits through modulus 100, not fineness or unbounded statements.

The 2016 fine-ring paper already determines fineness on every triangular representative, and its Example 5.6 already exhibits the exact trace-five matrix.
